subject: Post-demo: Data retention & 0-retention exception follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lloyd <sarah.lloyd@finsecure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: Data retention & 0-retention exception follow-up

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet your team this morning. Quick recap from our side and the immediate next steps we committed to: 

- Requirement: FinSecure asked about the ability to enforce a 0-retention policy for PII (user inputs) for a subset of routes (loan-verification API) and shortened logging for other production routes.
- Ask: Written confirmation of what Redwood can guarantee today vs. what would require Dedicated/Private deployment or a contractual addendum.
- Action items we promised:
  - Provide a short proposal that outlines options (0-retention for inputs, shortened logs, custom retention windows), and the tradeoffs (auditability, debugging, cost).
  - Share SOC2 summary and a suggested contract clause for retention exceptions.
  - Identify any feature or deployment requirement (e.g., Dedicated capacity / VPC) needed to meet 0-retention.

Attachments: 20260225-call-notes.pdf (agenda + notes).

Next steps: I will loop in Vivek (technical) and Rachel (CS) to propose a concrete, two-track approach: 1) immediate short-term controls we can document for hosted usage, and 2) an enterprise addendum for strict 0-retention routes (likely tied to Dedicated/Private).

Are you available for a 20-min sync Wednesday to review the proposed retention schedule?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Sarah Lloyd <sarah.lloyd@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@finsecure.com>, FinSecure Procurement <procurement@finsecure.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data retention & 0-retention exception follow-up

Thanks Marissa — great demo. A few clarifications from our side:

1) By 0-retention we mean that Alice (our loan ops users) inputs and any derived model context should not be persisted after the request completes. We need an auditable statement that the hosted endpoint does not write user content to any long-term logs or analytic stores.
2) For other routes (enrichment/transforms) we can accept a 7-day or 30-day short retention window for logs, but we need redaction of PII for anything stored.
3) Procurement wants to understand what contract language would look like (we will likely request an addendum). We also need SOC2 evidence and a pointer to how you handle audit logging (access logs) that we must retain for our compliance.

Can your team provide: a one-page tech summary, a proposed retention schedule we can put into an addendum, and the SOC2 summary? Also, any gating requirements (e.g., Dedicated instance) to achieve true 0-retention?

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Sarah
Sarah Lloyd, Director Product Security
FinSecure

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data retention & 0-retention exception follow-up

Quick technical notes (putting together the one-pager):

- Hosted (current Redwood API): we can 1) stop persisting request/response payloads to long-term analytic stores on a per-customer or per-route basis if customers opt-in, and 2) enable aggressive ephemeral caching eviction so KV caches do not persist beyond the request lifecycle. However, there are two caveats:
  a) Access/Audit logs (who called the API, timestamp, route) are still generated for operational and billing purposes. Those can be minimized to metadata (no payload) and retention shortened, but not fully disabled in hosted unless the customer moves to Dedicated/Private.
  b) Debugging/forensics: if 0-retention is enforced, reproducing issues is harder. We can offer temporary capture-on-demand windows for debugging with customer consent.
- Dedicated/Private: offering true 0-retention for payloads is straightforward when the customer controls the instance or when we provide an isolated runtime (no analytics pipeline ingestion).
- Short-term proposal: propose a two-tier schedule:
  1) Route-level 0-retention for PII inputs (no long-term storage), but audit logs (metadata-only) retained 30 days.
  2) Non-PII routes: 7-day or 30-day retention with optional PII redaction.

I'll draft the one-pager and the sample retention schedule for Marissa to share. Dev, can you provide suggested legal language for an addendum that allows exceptions and captures operational constraints?

—Vivek

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data retention & 0-retention exception follow-up

Marissa / team —

Draft legal takeaways:

1) We can agree to a contractual addendum that specifies retention behavior by route. Suggested clause: "Customer may designate specific API routes as "No-Persist"; Redwood will not persist request or response payloads for No-Persist routes to long-term analytic or training stores. Redwood will retain operational metadata (caller id, timestamp, route) for the purposes of billing, security, and abuse prevention for a mutually agreed-upon period."

2) Conditions: No-Persist commitments require either: (a) Dedicated/Private deployment or (b) explicit technical controls in hosted with written acceptance of limited debugging capability and a signed SLA exception. We should describe fallback support windows for forensic capture if needed.

3) Auditability: We can provide cryptographic proofs of non-retention (e.g., signed logs of deletion) as part of an enterprise package, but the specifics and cost need to be negotiated.

4) Proposed retention schedule: include three tiers — 0-retention (No-Persist), short retention (7 days), standard short-term (30 days). We will include redaction obligations and responsibilities for PII classification.

I'll attach a short draft clause and the retention schedule spreadsheet you can send to FinSecure.

—Dev Patel
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lloyd <sarah.lloyd@finsecure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, FinSecure Procurement <procurement@finsecure.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data retention & 0-retention exception follow-up

Hi Sarah / Mark / Procurement —

Following up with the materials we discussed: attached are the call notes, our SOC2 summary, and a proposed retention schedule + sample addendum (Data_Retention_Proposal_20260227.xlsx). High-level summary of options:

- Option A (Hosted + route-level No-Persist): Redwood will configure the customer account so selected routes are treated as No-Persist. No payloads will be written to long-term analytics/training stores. Operational metadata retained for 30 days by default (can be shortened to 14 days with a procurement/legal addendum). Debugging will be limited; we offer a capture-on-demand window for incident investigation.

- Option B (Dedicated/Private): Deploy model on Dedicated or Private instance to provide stronger guarantees (no analytics ingestion unless explicitly enabled). This is the recommended path for strict 0-retention plus required audit capabilities.

Next steps we propose:
1) Procurement: confirm which routes FinSecure wants No-Persist and which can be short retention (7/30 days).
2) Legal: sign the retention addendum (we will provide a redline-ready doc).
3) Tech: schedule a 30-min technical kickoff to document implementation details and timeline.

Proposed timeline: if procurement confirms routes by EOD next Thu (2026-03-04), we can turn on route-level No-Persist in hosted as a beta within 2 weeks, or schedule Dedicated deployment in 4-6 weeks depending on capacity.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/3698472) and shared draft (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDRP-Proposal).

Please confirm preferred next step and whether procurement needs any additional evidence for the addendum.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: Data_Retention_Proposal_20260227.xlsx, SOC2_summary.pdf, 20260225-call-notes.pdf
